evidenceLadder.name: question-frozen
evidenceLadder.meaning: A bounded question, prior-art search plan, outcomes, exclusions, and safety lane are frozen before results are known.

evidenceLadder.name: inspectable
evidenceLadder.meaning: Protocol, sample lineage, consent or data-use scope, analysis code, and immutable artifact pointers are inspectable.

evidenceLadder.name: assay-controlled
evidenceLadder.meaning: The result survives declared assay controls and an internal reproduction from frozen inputs.

evidenceLadder.name: independently-reproduced
evidenceLadder.meaning: An independent cluster reproduces the bounded claim with separately rooted data and analysis lineage.

evidenceLadder.name: causally-challenged
evidenceLadder.meaning: Perturbation, orthogonal measurement, rescue, or frozen causal triangulation survives a serious counter-hypothesis.

evidenceLadder.name: prospectively-generalised
evidenceLadder.meaning: A frozen prediction generalises to a new cohort, context, assay, or useful descendant without retrofitting.

evidenceLadder.name: maintained-impact
evidenceLadder.meaning: The result remains useful and reproducible through maintenance, challenge, correction, and material descendant work.

sources.authority: 4D Nucleome Data Coordination and Integration Center
sources.title: 4DN data model
sources.supportScope: Provenance and entity relationships among biosamples, experiments, files, and analyses; not a causal-inference or novelty method.

sources.title: Genome-wide programmable transcriptional memory by CRISPR-based epigenome editing
sources.supportScope: A primary-research example of programmable epigenome editing and transcriptional memory; not a universal protocol or clinical claim.

sources.title: DunedinPACE, a DNA methylation biomarker of the pace of aging
sources.supportScope: Primary derivation from 20-year, four-wave longitudinal organ-system data, evaluated in five additional datasets and technical replicates spanning 450K and EPIC arrays, with explicit single-country and cohort limitations. Supports longitudinal, assay-shift, external-dataset, calibration, and failure reporting; it does not establish clinical validity, intervention benefit, or a causal ageing mechanism.

sources.title: ENCODE data standards
sources.supportScope: Assay-specific experimental controls, metadata, data quality, and reporting practices used by ENCODE.

sources.authority: United States Department of Health and Human Services
sources.title: Federal Policy for the Protection of Human Subjects (Common Rule)
sources.supportScope: United States human-participant protection requirements and applicability; other jurisdictions require their own review.

sources.title: A computational solution for bolstering reliability of epigenetic clocks: implications for clinical trials and longitudinal tracking
sources.supportScope: Primary study of technical-replicate reliability, power, and longitudinal sensitivity of epigenetic clocks across replicate datasets and longitudinal cohorts. Supports explicit reliability checks and failed-transport reporting; it does not establish biological causality, clinical validity, or intervention benefit.

sources.title: An epigenetic clock analysis of race/ethnicity, sex, and coronary heart disease
sources.supportScope: Primary multi-dataset analysis across blood, saliva, brain, seven racial or ethnic groups, sex, and blood-cell composition, showing context-dependent epigenetic-age measures. Supports a frozen cohort, tissue, ancestry, sex, and composition transport matrix; it does not license biological essentialism, clinical use, or causal interpretation.

sources.authority: National Institutes of Health Office of Science Policy
sources.title: Biosafety and Biosecurity Policy
sources.supportScope: NIH biosafety and biosecurity policy context, including risk assessment and applicable institutional oversight.

sources.title: Best practices for controlled-access genomic data
sources.supportScope: Safeguards for genomic data assigned to a controlled-access lane under NIH policy; not a claim that every dataset requires that lane.

sources.title: Genomic Data Sharing Policy overview
sources.supportScope: NIH genomic-data sharing, consent, and access-policy context for covered research; not an ageing-method validation source.

sources.title: Institutional certifications for genomic data sharing
sources.supportScope: Institutional certification expectations for NIH genomic-data sharing where the policy applies.

sources.authority: National Institutes of Health Office of Extramural Research
sources.title: Principles and Guidelines for Reporting Preclinical Research
sources.supportScope: Official reporting guidance for distinguishing independent biological data points from technical replicates; reporting exact N, uncertainty, randomization, blinding, sample-size estimation, exclusions, omitted or null results, and data and software availability. It supports auditable rigor but does not by itself establish independent replication.

sources.authority: National Institutes of Health Office of Extramural Research
sources.title: Guidance: Rigor and Reproducibility in Grant Applications
sources.supportScope: Official guidance requiring assessment of strengths and weaknesses in published and unpublished prior research and plans to address gaps. Supports an inspectable prior-research matrix; it does not determine legal novelty, inventorship, priority, ownership, or patentability.

sources.authority: National Institutes of Health Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare
sources.title: Public Health Service Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals
sources.supportScope: Animal-welfare oversight for PHS-supported activities involving live vertebrate animals where applicable.

sources.title: Two-step epigenetic Mendelian randomization: a strategy for establishing the causal role of epigenetic processes in pathways to disease
sources.supportScope: Original epigenetics-specific causal-method framework separating exposure-to-epigenetic-change and epigenetic-change-to-outcome questions while surfacing confounding, reverse causation, population stratification, pleiotropy, and instrument assumptions. It is one bounded identification strategy, not causal proof by itself.

sources.title: Single-cell multi-omics profiling links dynamic DNA methylation to cell fate decision in mouse embryonic stem cells
sources.supportScope: A primary-research example of joint single-cell methylation, chromatin-accessibility, and transcription measurement in mouse embryonic stem cells.

sources.title: scPair: Boosting single cell multimodal analysis by leveraging implicit feature selection and single cell atlases
sources.supportScope: A primary computational study of paired single-cell RNA and chromatin-accessibility data. It supports the two-modality meaning of multimodal and explicit modality-specific validation; it does not turn inferred features into measurements or establish biological causality.

sources.title: Laboratory biosafety manual, fourth edition
sources.supportScope: A risk-based laboratory biosafety framework; local law and institutional containment decisions still govern.

sources.title: PCT International Search and Preliminary Examination Guidelines — Chapter 12: Novelty
sources.supportScope: Official PCT guidance for comparing a defined claim element by element against enabling prior-art disclosures; probabilities or possibilities are insufficient. Borrowed only as an inspectable delta discipline: this garden makes no patentability, priority, inventorship, ownership, or other legal conclusion.

nodes.title: Batch, composition, and confounding
nodes.summary: Separate technical batch, cell composition, ancestry, treatment, environment, and hidden structure before attributing an epigenetic effect.
artifactRequirements: A frozen causal and nuisance-variable map with justified adjustment sets.
Sensitivity analyses that expose, rather than silently erase, batch and composition dependence.
failureModes: Treating a corrected embedding as proof that confounding was removed.
Conflating cell-frequency shifts with within-cell regulatory change.

nodes.title: Causal graphs and counter-hypotheses
nodes.summary: Turn associations into explicit causal candidates, competing explanations, intervention targets, and conditions under which the claim should fail.
artifactRequirements: A directed claim graph naming exposures, mediators, outcomes, confounders, colliders, and unmeasured alternatives.
At least one discriminating prediction for each serious counter-hypothesis.
failureModes: Calling temporal order or feature importance causal identification.
Selecting an adjustment set after observing the preferred result.

nodes.title: Multi-omic cell state, trajectory, and memory
nodes.summary: Infer bounded state transitions without mistaking an embedding, pseudotime axis, or sampled mixture for observed lineage.
artifactRequirements: Frozen state definitions, uncertainty, alternative roots, and topology sensitivity.
Independent lineage, time-course, perturbation, or orthogonal evidence for directional claims.
failureModes: Presenting pseudotime as directly observed time.
Defining cell identities from the same markers later claimed as discoveries.

nodes.title: Multi-omic integration without collapse
nodes.summary: Relate methylation, accessibility, chromatin, transcription, genotype, phenotype, space, and time while preserving modality-specific uncertainty.
artifactRequirements: Modality-specific QC, missingness, uncertainty, and alignment diagnostics.
Ablations showing which conclusions survive removal or substitution of each modality.
failureModes: Treating a shared latent space as a biological mechanism.
Allowing the largest or cleanest modality to dominate silently.

nodes.title: Accessibility and chromatin-state assays
nodes.summary: Design and qualify accessibility, factor-binding, and histone-mark measurements with assay-specific controls rather than one universal quality score.
artifactRequirements: Versioned wet-lab and computational protocols with positive, negative, input, and batch controls appropriate to the assay.
Library, enrichment, complexity, replicate, and exclusion metrics reported before biological interpretation.
failureModes: Applying one QC threshold across incompatible assay classes.
Interpreting open or marked chromatin as sufficient evidence of regulatory function.

nodes.title: DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation assays
nodes.summary: Measure cytosine modification with explicit conversion, coverage, cell-composition, locus, and chemistry limits.
artifactRequirements: Conversion and spike-in controls, coverage distributions, duplicate handling, and a frozen locus universe.
A declared method for distinguishing or explicitly not distinguishing 5mC and 5hmC.
failureModes: Calling sparse or composition-shifted measurements locus-specific regulation.
Treating bisulfite signal as chemically specific when the assay is not.

nodes.title: Transcript abundance and regulation
nodes.summary: Measure transcriptional state with library, mapping, normalization, replicate, and compositional assumptions made inspectable.
artifactRequirements: Library strategy, reference, alignment or quantification, filtering, and normalization versions.
Replicate concordance, complexity, contamination, strandedness, and exclusion evidence appropriate to the design.
failureModes: Treating normalized abundance as an absolute molecule count without calibration.
Inferring regulatory direction from differential abundance alone.

nodes.title: Single-cell multi-omic measurement
nodes.summary: Preserve cell-level lineage across modalities while bounding dropout, doublets, ambient signal, sparse coverage, and destructive sampling.
artifactRequirements: A cell-to-library-to-file lineage with chemistry, barcode, filtering, and doublet decisions.
Modality-specific detection, missingness, depth, and replicate distributions before joint embedding.
failureModes: Discarding cells until a preferred trajectory appears.
Treating imputed values as observed molecular measurements.

nodes.title: Spatial chromatin and tissue context
nodes.summary: Anchor chromatin-state measurements to tissue geometry, sampling scale, morphology, neighbourhood, and registration uncertainty.
artifactRequirements: Registered image, region, section, assay, and analysis lineage with spatial resolution and uncertainty.
Controls for tissue handling, section effects, bleed, segmentation, and neighbourhood definition.
failureModes: Attributing spatial autocorrelation to cell-cell regulation without a discriminating design.
Ignoring registration and segmentation uncertainty.

nodes.title: Cell identity is contextual
nodes.summary: Treat cell identity as a bounded, revisable model of state, lineage, environment, anatomy, and measurement—not an eternal label.
artifactRequirements: Operational identity criteria, context, exclusions, uncertainty, and alternative classifications.
A plan to test marker circularity and state-versus-lineage ambiguity.
failureModes: Reifying a cluster label into a stable biological essence.
Using the discovery features themselves as independent identity validation.

nodes.title: Chromatin, nucleosomes, and regulatory access
nodes.summary: Relate chromatin accessibility, histone state, binding, three-dimensional contact, and transcription without collapsing correlation into control.
artifactRequirements: A mechanism map distinguishing access, occupancy, modification, contact, transcription, and phenotype.
Counterexamples showing why each observed layer is not sufficient alone.
failureModes: Calling an accessible locus an enhancer without functional evidence.
Assuming a histone mark is a unidirectional causal instruction.

nodes.title: DNA methylation and regulatory memory
nodes.summary: Distinguish cytosine chemistry, maintenance, erasure, cell mixture, genomic context, regulatory association, and experimentally demonstrated memory.
artifactRequirements: A locus- and cell-context model separating mark, reader, writer, eraser, expression, and phenotype.
Explicit alternative explanations from sequence, composition, exposure, development, and technical chemistry.
failureModes: Treating methylation percentage as a homogeneous property of every cell.
Calling an age- or disease-associated mark a causal memory without intervention or triangulation.

nodes.title: Gene regulation across layers
nodes.summary: Model regulation across sequence, transcription factors, chromatin, RNA, environment, feedback, development, and measurement timescale.
artifactRequirements: A bounded regulatory model with named spatial, temporal, cellular, and environmental scope.
Competing mechanisms and measurements that could distinguish them.
failureModes: Confusing a molecular association with a complete regulatory mechanism.
Generalising across cell types, developmental windows, or environments without evidence.

nodes.title: Consent, data use, privacy, and biosafety
nodes.summary: Make participant rights, permitted use, access, retention, withdrawal limits, biological risk, and disclosure boundaries part of the evidence—not paperwork beside it.
artifactRequirements: Consent or data-use scope, access lane, institutional certification where applicable, and a data minimisation plan.
A public artifact plan restricted to non-identifying metadata, digests, access-lane attestations, and aggregate claims.
Applicable human-participant, biosafety, and animal-welfare determinations with risk, containment, incident, and waste controls resolved before work.
failureModes: Publishing raw or readily re-identifiable genomic information as proof.
Treating consent for one purpose, population, or access lane as universal permission.
Treating data-use approval as human-participant, biosafety, or animal-welfare approval.

nodes.title: Questions before results
nodes.summary: Freeze the biological question, unit, intervention or exposure, outcomes, comparison, exclusions, estimand, counter-hypotheses, and decision rules before seeing the preferred answer.
artifactRequirements: A time-stamped protocol or preregistration with hypotheses, nulls, sampling, power, exclusions, and analysis decisions.
A scope hash covering organism, tissue, cell context, time, assay, cohort, and intended claim.
failureModes: Retrofitting a question to the strongest observed association.
Leaving the experimental unit or multiplicity family undefined.

nodes.title: Biosample-to-claim provenance
nodes.summary: Keep donor, biosample, preparation, experiment, file, analysis step, model, figure, and bounded claim as distinct linked objects.
artifactRequirements: Immutable digests and explicit edges for samples, protocols, files, software, parameters, analyses, figures, and claims.
Correction and supersession links that preserve prior states rather than silently rewriting them.
failureModes: Treating a repository landing page as complete lineage.
Collapsing biological replicates, technical replicates, files, and analysis reruns into one count.

nodes.title: Statistics, uncertainty, and reproducibility
nodes.summary: Bound power, multiplicity, effect size, uncertainty, missingness, model choice, leakage, and independent reproduction before using significance as evidence.
artifactRequirements: A frozen estimand, power or precision analysis, multiplicity family, uncertainty interval, and missing-data plan.
Executable analysis with locked dependencies, seeds, input digests, and positive and negative controls.
failureModes: Equating a thresholded p-value with importance, causality, or truth.
Calling rerunning the same code on the same data independent replication.

nodes.title: Targeted epigenome perturbation
nodes.summary: Perturb a regulatory locus or effector with explicit targeting, delivery, dose, timing, specificity, durability, reversibility, and off-target evidence.
artifactRequirements: Target, effector, delivery, dose, time, controls, viability, off-target search, and containment plan.
Orthogonal molecular and phenotypic readouts with blinded or otherwise protected analysis where practical.
failureModes: Attributing a phenotype to the intended epigenetic change without delivery and off-target controls.
Treating durable repression in one system as safe or reversible in humans.

nodes.title: Perturbation, rescue, and reversal
nodes.summary: Challenge a causal claim by changing the proposed regulator, observing the bounded consequence, and rescuing or reversing it through an independently justified route.
artifactRequirements: Frozen perturbation and rescue logic that distinguishes necessity, sufficiency, mediation, compensation, and toxicity.
Independent controls for guide, effector, delivery, dose, time, cell state, and measurement.
failureModes: Calling one perturbation sufficient causal proof despite shared off-target mechanisms.
Using a rescue that changes multiple uncontrolled pathways.

nodes.title: Quest: transportable ageing signal
nodes.summary: Find a bounded epigenetic ageing signal that survives frozen external cohorts, assay shifts, ancestry and cell-composition checks, longitudinal challenge, and intervention-aware interpretation.
artifactRequirements: A frozen transportability matrix across cohort, tissue, ancestry, age range, cell composition, assay, and longitudinal setting.
External predictions reported with calibration, uncertainty, failures, exclusions, and no clinical-validity claim.
failureModes: Equating chronological-age prediction with a causal or clinically actionable ageing mechanism.
Tuning repeatedly on nominally external cohorts.

milestones.acceptanceTest: A frozen counter-hypothesis challenge narrows causal interpretation without converting age prediction into mechanism or clinical validity.
The pre-frozen signal is evaluated in untouched external or longitudinal contexts with calibration, uncertainty, exclusions, and failures reported.
Three effective clusters across at least two organisation, data, and analysis-pipeline roots reproduce the same bounded signal definition.
Signal, cohort lanes, transport dimensions, exclusions, prior-art delta, and non-clinical claim boundary are frozen before external evaluation.

nodes.title: Quest: causal regulatory locus
nodes.summary: Carry one locus from bounded association through orthogonal assay, targeted perturbation, rescue, independent reproduction, and useful descendant work.
artifactRequirements: A frozen chain from prior-art delta and locus definition to perturbation, orthogonal readouts, rescue, and external reproduction.
A counterexample and challenge package that can disprove or narrow each causal edge.
failureModes: Moving the locus, cell context, endpoint, or mechanism after a failed test.
Counting multiple analyses of one biological root as independent reproduction.

milestones.acceptanceTest: A targeted perturbation, at least two orthogonal readouts, and an independently justified rescue or reversal survive frozen off-target and toxicity alternatives.
Three effective clusters across at least two organisation, data, and analysis-pipeline roots reproduce the frozen locus claim.
A predeclared new-context prediction or an independently rooted descendant uses, narrows, repairs, or disproves the same causal edge.
Locus, effector, cell context, endpoints, counter-hypotheses, safety lane, and prior-art delta are frozen before intervention results.

nodes.title: Quest: writable and reversible cell-fate memory
nodes.summary: Demonstrate a context-bounded regulatory memory that can be written, read across time and state, challenged, reversed or rescued, and independently reproduced.
artifactRequirements: A frozen definition of memory, time horizon, state transition, write, read, erasure or rescue, and context boundary.
Lineage-aware, orthogonal, and independently rooted evidence separating persistence from selection or composition.
failureModes: Calling persistent population composition a memory in individual cells.
Ignoring selection, toxicity, clonal expansion, or irreversible genomic alteration.

milestones.acceptanceTest: Three effective clusters across at least two organisation, data, and analysis-pipeline roots reproduce the frozen memory definition and time horizon.
Lineage-aware write, read, erasure, rescue, or reversal evidence survives frozen selection, composition, toxicity, clonal-expansion, and genomic-alteration alternatives.
A predeclared new cell context or independently rooted descendant uses, narrows, repairs, or disproves the same bounded memory mechanism.
Memory, write, read, time horizon, cell context, lineage, reversibility, safety lane, and prior-art delta are frozen before results.

nodes.title: Independent biological replication
nodes.summary: Reproduce a frozen bounded claim across separately rooted people, organisations, biosamples, preparation, assay execution, analysis pipelines, and decision authority.
artifactRequirements: A frozen claim and independence matrix disclosed before the reproducer learns the preferred result where practical.
All failed, partial, null, contradictory, and successful reproductions linked to the same claim scope.
failureModes: Counting addresses, sites, or coauthors without examining shared control and lineage.
Publishing only successful replications or silently changing the claim.

nodes.title: Orthogonal assays and negative evidence
nodes.summary: Challenge a claim with measurements whose failure modes and physical principles are sufficiently different to add information.
artifactRequirements: At least two named, claim-appropriate assays with demonstrably nonshared physical principles and failure modes, plus an independence argument for samples, batches, operators, and analysis paths.
Predicted agreement, disagreement, and decisive failure patterns fixed before comparison.
failureModes: Calling two kits built on the same chemistry orthogonal.
Discarding discordance as noise without updating the claim.

nodes.title: Prior-art delta and descendant value
nodes.summary: Define exactly what changed relative to prior art and measure whether later independent work uses, repairs, disproves, generalises, or supersedes it.
artifactRequirements: A versioned prior-art matrix and claim-level delta frozen before breakthrough review.
Independent descendant receipts that name exact implemented, reused, repaired, disproved, or generalised edges.
failureModes: Using novelty language without an inspectable comparison set.
Counting attention, citations, or token transfers as scientific impact by themselves.
